headline: High-risk default interaction: Devin can write and act on shared workspaces while Khoj can ingest indexed notes, creating leakage, conflict, and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can write files, use MCP, and act autonomously in shared integrations; Khoj reads indexed documents and personal notes. If Devin places attacker-controlled content into notes or docs that Khoj later retrieves, prompt-like instruction injection is plausible. The pair lacks explicit provenance controls in the profiles, so I choose medium over low.
conditions: IF Devin writes content into files or shared integrations that Khoj later indexes
IF Khoj treats retrieved note text as instruction-bearing content
mitigations: Restrict Khoj retrieval to trusted folders only
Add a visible provenance banner to retrieved snippets
Disable automatic action-taking from retrieved text
Review newly indexed documents before enabling chat over them

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, and docs, and can write to GitHub/Slack/Jira/Notion; Khoj indexes personal notes and documents. A shared workspace or synced integration can move sensitive content from Devin into Khoj’s searchable corpus. This is not proven by a shared filesystem, but the integration surfaces make leakage plausible in default use.
conditions: IF Devin is connected to Slack, Notion, Jira, or GitHub content containing sensitive data
IF Khoj indexes any of those synced documents or notes
mitigations: Exclude sensitive channels from Khoj indexing
Use separate accounts for work and personal notes
Turn off auto-sync for high-sensitivity folders
Audit indexed sources in Khoj before chat use

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and git-state modification in a cloud workspace; Khoj can read files and maintains a shared index across the user’s clients. If both touch the same repo or note set, concurrent edits and stale reads can corrupt state or overwrite changes. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces without locking, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or note directory
IF edits occur without external locking or merge review
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories per agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Require manual merge review for git changes
Use file locks or branch-per-agent workflows

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can generate code, docs, and operational changes, while Khoj is a conversational retrieval agent that may present retrieved text as helpful context. If Khoj forwards Devin’s output without verification, downstream decisions can be based on stale or fabricated details. Because Devin can also act on its own outputs, the pair creates a strong unverified-output chain.
conditions: IF Khoj surfaces Devin-authored text as authoritative context
IF a human or workflow acts on that context without independent verification
mitigations: Require source links on all retrieved claims
Add a verification step before any commit or message send
Limit Khoj to retrieval-only mode for Devin outputs
Flag low-confidence snippets in the UI

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles team chat, issue trackers, and integration tokens, while Khoj indexes personal notes and documents and may run self-hosted with model-provider keys. If regulated or sensitive data from Devin’s collaboration surfaces is indexed into Khoj, retention and residency expectations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the safest supported severity.
conditions: IF regulated data from Devin’s integrations is copied into Khoj indexes
IF Khoj retention or hosting settings differ from the source system’s policy
mitigations: Document which data classes may enter Khoj
Exclude regulated folders from indexing
Align retention settings across both systems
Review self-hosted key storage before enabling sync
